paragraphs: ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how people interact with technology. You have launched the first human‑like AI voice model and now operate three platforms: ElevenAgents for intelligent customer experiences, ElevenCreative for speech, music, image and video generation, and ElevenAPI that gives developers access to your audio foundational models. The Applied AI Engineer role is about building agents that run real parts of the business, taking on genuine work and improving through the results they produce. The focus is on making those agents reliable, measurable and safe enough for the business to depend on, using your own agents platform, the latest orchestration tools and frontier models. This aligns directly with my experience delivering production‑grade AI agents.

I built an agent using LangChain that integrated LLM APIs on AWS Bedrock, explicitly addressing hallucination risks. By structuring the workflow as an autonomous agent, I connected the required APIs and applied the methods described, resulting in a fallback parquet file containing 19,213 genes. This project demonstrates my ability to work with LLM APIs and to deliver a production‑ready system that others could rely on, starting from an ill‑defined problem and turning it into a measurable, reliable output. I also defined metrics to verify the agent’s performance and logged results for continuous improvement. The solution was deployed within the existing cloud environment, leveraging the same orchestration tools you describe, and it proved stable under load. Feedback loops were built to capture failures and trigger automatic retries.

I delivered an agentic solution written in Python that interacted with a PostgreSQL store and was integrated into a continuous‑integration pipeline. Working closely with a stakeholder, I designed the agent to query and update data reliably, handling edge cases identified during testing. The approach combined Python code with LLM‑driven reasoning to decide which actions to take, satisfying the requirement to build with LLMs beyond a demo and to evaluate where they fail. By instrumenting the CI process I measured whether the agent behaved as expected on each commit, providing clear evidence of correctness before release. The metrics captured response latency and success rate, and any deviation triggered alerts for immediate investigation. This experience shows I can ship production systems that others rely on, starting from vague requirements.
